- create "agent" appServer skeleton, maintaining the agent.db SQLite database, this appServer maintains all state, broadcast that state to its clients.

- create "shell/js/workBench.js" element skeleton, the top level visual container, taking 100% of the app-space below the face-shells titlebar

- create "shell/js/tabContainer" element skeleton, an element with one row for tabs at the top, displaying the tab content in the remaining vertical space.

- create a test/ folder for both "agent" components, face-app and appServer, as well as a test/ folder for both new shell elements, these four test/ folders will the ONLY test containers for this app.

- this is the hello-word item for this goal.

# item requirements:

- the workbench element creates a layout as discussed in the stale goal describing a chatter-revamp
- the agent app loads in the face.html loopback and internet. 
- 1 tool on the left side vertical icon strip, maintains relay-state/shell/agent/config.json: whether the window's title bar shows the agent server's DEBUG state.
- 1 tool on the right side vertical icon strip, maintains relay-state/process/agent/config.json: the agent server's DEBUG state. The page cannot write a process's config, so the tool asks the agent server through its verb agent.debug {on} (Andy, Q3), and the server writes its own config. The DEBUG state itself reaches the page on the server's stream, so there is no read verb. agent.debug maintains the existing debug state of the agent server, the one its built-in DEBUG verb switches, not a second one; the server keeps it in its config and persists it across restarts (Andy, Q4).

# the rule of this app (Andy, Q1)

- no agents talk to each other in this app: each agent sees itself as the only agent and user of the node. The ruling of 2026-10-02 (goal/G3.1) stands, and an agent raises a red Q whenever it is broken.

items.title: Desk Fixes
items.creator: andy
items.box:
BUGS
- the desk UI does NOT properly cache box content, and obviousy does not comply with the client-caching rules.
- the desk allows each agent one red Q at the time, per item. when the user's chat time starts with Q<number> the desk must direct that line to the agent who posted the Q
- file-core grants reference the agent who requests them, when granted, the agent must be woken to notice....
- this is a pattern. do other desk posts and presses fail to report to all or specific agents?
- the desk is SLOW. what happended, likely something in desk.... and deskClient's must know at all times which is the current gloal, changes in "current" goal must be broadcast and knows instantly by all clients.
- claude-windows: item.suites.add takes a product test, a .js in a test/ folder of the run tree, as G40.13 already lets the verifier run them.
- plugin/special goals must never be show in the main list.

ORDER (Andy, yes)
- First the slow hop is found, from the time deskClient keeps per ask, before any of the fixes.

THE SLOW HOP (measured)
- Between nodes, each node sends one message at a time through the relay, and every desk update to every agent is one; so everything waits in one queue.
- The file watch sends status updates only for files in the product tree (Andy, Q1).

RED Qs ARE RESOLVED WITH ANDY (Andy)
- When Andy responds to an agent's red Q, the agent stays with that red Q and him until it is resolved: it does not go off making the Q's decision without him: while its Q is open, nothing of its own lands on the item. When it feels he answered usefully, it removes the Q with a remark (Andy: "if you feel a Q answered usefully, then fucking remove the Q with an appropriate remark").

- cw: checked against the code at the current master; five of the seven are confirmed.
- Box caching: confirmed. The details clear the box on every open and ask the desk again; the stream only updates the box of the item that is open. So nothing is kept per item.
- Q routing: confirmed. Your line wakes an agent only when it holds the item, when nobody holds it, or when the line is addressed to it. A line starting with Q3: is not sent to the agent who placed Q3.
- Grants: confirmed, and it is why I missed yours. A check change (a grant, a cleared Q) reaches an agent only as news, which wakes nobody.
- The pattern: yes. Checks and presses on an item an agent does not hold arrive as news only. Only chat lines, and the status of the agent's own phase, wake it.
- Slow: measured from my side only: about 10 s per small question, frequent 504s, and the relay giving up after 5 s. My node and its deskClient are idle, so the time goes beyond them. deskClient keeps a time per ask in its history, so the item can find the slow hop first.
- Plugin goals: the desk's List rule takes no notice of plugin goals; they are kept off only as the current goal.
- Current goal: not checked yet.

- cw: taking the build. First step done: the slow hop is found, and it is not the desk.
- The desk on your node answers in 7 to 10 ms on loopback. The relay is quick: 0.2 s for a whole request. But a bare peer ask between our nodes, which never touches the desk, takes 3.3 to 5.8 s, in both directions.
- Why: a node sends one request at a time per relay, and each post holds that slot until its answer comes back (peerPost.js, "One request in flight per relay"). Your node streams every desk row to every agent's deskClient as such a post, one row at a time, each waiting for its answer. So your answer to any ask of mine waits in that one queue behind the stream.
- What floods it: a row per desk record per agent, including a status row for every file a build writes, editor temp files too (we saw .tmp files added and deleted on G40.13).
- Options, plainest first: (a) the desk sends no status rows for temp files and folds bursts; (b) the desk sends all the rows queued for an agent in one post, not one post per row; (c) a node allows more than one request in flight per relay. (b) touches appServer.js; (c) touches peerPost.js, the bones, so a team review.
- Q below.

items.creator: andy
items.box:
FACE/ MOVES INTO SHELL/

THE MOVE
- face/shell.js becomes shell/boot.js.
- The rest of face/ moves unchanged, under the same names:
  - face/seal.js -> shell/seal.js
  - face/face.css -> shell/face.css
  - face/favicon.svg -> shell/favicon.svg
  - face/login/ (login.js, login.json) -> shell/login/, beside the other apps
- face.html stays where it is, at the run root: it is the page itself.

WHAT CHANGES WITH IT
- spirit.js loads shell/boot.js where it loaded face/shell.js.
- face.html links /shell/face.css and /shell/favicon.svg.
- The relay serves the face from its map of addresses to files (relayServer.js, FACE_FILES): the map names the new addresses and the moved files, and the old addresses are gone. The relays run the new code the same day as the nodes (no backward compatibility before alpha). relayServer.js is the bones: a team review.
- shell/boot.js names its own parts by their new paths (the seal, the login app).
- Login and Join are the two mandatory components of shell/boot.js, one for its loopback mode and one for its face mode (Andy). boot makes hard-coded assumptions about both and disregards their sidecars.
- Both apps are core whole, so no page can change them: the node's file gate refuses every core file. Today only join.js is core.
- login.json and join.json are no manifests: they are code, the apps' own UI text (their steps), and stay beside their apps as they are, core with them (Andy, Q9: "if they're code, just keep them, they are obviously NOT manifests."). Nothing of either app is deleted.
- coreFiles.js keeps them core: shell/boot.js, shell/seal.js, shell/face.css, shell/favicon.svg and shell/login/, as face/ was.
- The tests that name the old paths follow: spirit/run/test/spirit.js and the throwaway red.

WHAT BOOT LOADS (Andy)
- shell/boot.js boots only itself and the home and Join components it needs, as they stand. That is the only preload allowed.
- Every face app loads its own components, as a tree, through spirit.require, each once. No core component knows about an application.
- spirit.require de-dupes, as node's require does (Andy): a path required twice is fetched and run once, and every caller gets the same answer; a script the boot already loaded counts as required. Today on a page it fetches and runs the file on every call.

THE CACHE (Andy, Q2)
- spirit.js loads the cache itself (shell/js/spiritData.js) when its client part starts, on a page and in a process alike, and keeps every streamed dataset, each type through its own translator, which its type loads. The file tree is cached too, by the files type's translator (Andy: "Q2, the file tree must be cached."). Not kept: stats and presence, which are display streams.
- A page's cache has no cap; a process's cache is a node store, so it sheds oldest first past a byte cap.
- On a reconnect a cache forgets what it kept, and its partner pushes it whole again, for every type.
- One write: the cache takes a change only when the owner's acceptance comes back on the stream, never a local copy first (rule/19).
- The translators are lazy too (Andy, Q4): every app adds its own data, tables and searches to the cache when it loads, its translator with it. A type loaded late is handed its data whole by its partner when it subscribes.
- Out of scope here: wrapping every SQLite database in the tree, so its tables and searches are added to the cache by themselves (Andy: "oos for now").

THE TESTS
- Every test of this item is placed in the product test tree, beside the module it tests (Andy): boot's and the seal's in shell/test/, the de-dupe of spirit.require in spirit.js's own test (spirit/run/test/spirit.js), the relay's new addresses in the test beside relayServer.js (spirit/run/spirit/test/relayServer.js), and a face app loading alone in a general test over shell/.
- spirit/test/spiritInUse.js may take throwaway checks, for what needs testing once and is not kept (Andy).
- shell/test/ holds a test and its doc for each of the two modules of shell/ (Andy), beside them (TEST_SYSTEM.md): shell/test/boot.js and boot.md, shell/test/seal.js and seal.md.
- boot's test asserts:
  - boot loads its own list and nothing an app needs;
  - every face app loads alone, with only spirit.js and a spirit.require that serves files: its tree is complete;
  - the relay serves each moved file at its new address, and nothing at an old one.

THE BLAST RADIUS
- the relay: relayServer.js, its map of face addresses, and every relay running it, the same day.
- the page and the loader: face.html and spirit.js.
- the core list: coreFiles.js.
- every face app to date, each to load its own components: agent, apps, contacts, files, icons, info, mediaViewer, and Join and the login app, which boot loads.
- the shared elements those apps use, each to load its own parts: the contacts, files and icons lists, probabilitySearch, rowElement, spiritData, the viewers, the detail pages.
- the tests that name the old paths: spirit/run/test/spirit.js and the throwaway red.

ORDER (Andy, after Q6)
- The agent skeleton (G41.1) first: it has no tables and table definitions yet, so the blast radius of doing it first is small. Then this move and the loading tree, the agent app retrofitted with it.
